study.title: Deep learning for estimating right ventricular function from routine coronary angiography

imaging.modality_detail: Routine cine coronary angiography of the right coronary artery (LAO and RAO projections)
imaging.territory_detail: Right coronary artery angiograms used to estimate right ventricular systolic function
imaging.frames_per_sequence: First 72 frames extracted, first 15 removed; 16 to 48 frames tested as model input

data_released.detail: Data cannot be shared publicly; de-identified data may be made available upon reasonable request subject to data use agreements

annotation.annotator_expertise: Labels derived from RV systolic function documented on transthoracic echocardiogram within 30 days

task.task_description: Binary classification of right ventricular systolic function (normal vs abnormal; any RV dysfunction >=mild and significant RV dysfunction >=mild-moderate) from two RCA cine angiograms (LAO and RAO) using two X3D 3D CNNs fused by an MLP; also an ensemble with an ECG-based model and survival analysis of model predictions.
task.clinical_application: Opportunistic real-time screening for RV dysfunction in the cath lab during routine coronary angiography

temporal_evidence.quote: Our proposed approach includes two 3D CNNs (each of which accepts one cine image per patient as input), concatenates their outcome, passes through a multilayer perceptron (MLP)

G2.quote: we did not perform external validation of the algorithms for 2 reasons (a) the inability to identify a sufficiently large external dataset with angiography and RV function assessment

G6.quote: The clinical usefulness of these data requires validation in prospective studies.

G7.quote: To investigate the model interpretability, Grad-CAM activation maps were generated for the two utilized projections

G8.quote: our study is the first to document that using multi-input data (ECG and angiography) readily available in the Cath lab during angiography is superior to a single input

G9.quote: we were unable to evaluate model performance in patients with specific high-risk conditions such as acute STEMI or pulmonary embolism

G11.quote: the presence of RV dysfunction identified by the AI tool was associated with higher allcause mortality

other_limitations: Echocardiography as imperfect reference standard for RV function
30-day window between echocardiography and angiography may introduce bias
Variability in echo assessment of RV function across labs
Heart rate at angiography not consistently available
future_work: External validation via research consortia or recurring local validation
Prospective pragmatic study of clinical utility
Combining angiography with invasive haemodynamic parameters
Single procedural dashboard integrating RV, LV dysfunction and LV filling pressure models
Evaluation in high-risk subgroups such as STEMI and pulmonary embolism
